title: Sharp Internal Divided Differences in RIG Calculus Critical Integrals, Quarter-Order Regularity, and Node Coalescence
content: We study real internal divided differences on the Hilbert completion of commutative square-zero path algebras, with the normalized path basis orthonormal.  A recursive multiplication estimate gives exact finite-depth maxima and depth-uniform suprema for arbitrary homogeneous multi-node divided differences.  On quadratic inputs, positive averages of the exponential are bounded on the critical ball of radius \(1/\sqrt{2}\) precisely when their endpoint mass satisfies an explicit square-tail integral criterion.  Fractional exponential integrals have a sharp quarter-order threshold, exact derivative norm formulae, optimal Hölder exponents and logarithmic endpoint moduli.  We determine the finite-depth growth at the threshold and show that the number of strictly subcritical nodes determines the differentiability of exponential divided differences.  The one-sided critical secant has sharp constant \(2\sqrt{1-\log 2}\); approaching equal critical node radii gives an explicit fourth-root divergence law.  Every fixed quadratic input still has a real-analytic exponential on a neighborhood.
